knowledge_point.title: Determining the Equation of a Normal Line to a Curve at a Point

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2 x^{2} + 2 x + 1$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=4 x + 2
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(-1\right)=4 \left(-1\right) + 2=-2
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(-2\right)}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(1\right)&=\frac{1}{2}\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{2}+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+\left(1\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{2} + \frac{3}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $a=\frac{1}{2}$ and $b=\frac{3}{2}$.

Find the slope $m'$ of the normal line to the curve

$$
y=(x+2)(x^{2}-3x)
$$

at the point $\left(-1,4\right)$. Give an exact answer.

$m'=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=(x+2)(x^{2}-3x)$. Expand and combine like terms before differentiating.

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=x^{3}-3x^{2}+2x^{2}-6x\\
&=x^{3}-x^{2}-6x
\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the power rule:

$$
f'(x)=3x^{2}-2x-6
$$

The tangent slope at $\left(-1,4\right)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}
m=f'(-1)&=3\left(-1\right)^{2}-2\left(-1\right)-6\\
&=3+2-6\\
&=-1
\end{aligned}
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so take the negative reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}
m'&=-\frac{1}{m}\\
&=-\frac{1}{\left(-1\right)}\\
&=1
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$

\end{aligned}

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$.

\end{aligned}

The intersection is $(-74,0)$.

The intersection is $(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$. Give exact values.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Differentiate the polynomial.

$$
f'(x)=- 3 x^{2}.
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(1)&=- 3 (1)^{2}=-3, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{(-3)}=\frac{1}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(1,-4)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(-4)&=\frac{1}{3}(x-(1)), \\y&=\frac{x}{3} - \frac{13}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=\frac{1}{3}x+\left(- \frac{13}{3}\right), \\x&=13.
\end{aligned}
$$

The intersection is $(13,0)$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
First find the point on the curve.

$$
f(4)=-2\sqrt{(4)}-2(4)+1=-11.
$$

The normal passes through $(4,-11)$.

Rewrite the radical or reciprocal using powers, then differentiate.

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=- 2 x^{\frac{1}{2}} - 2 x + 1, \\f'(x)&=-2 - \frac{1}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}}=-2 - \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(4)&=-2 - \frac{1}{\sqrt{(4)}}=- \frac{5}{2}, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{\left(- \frac{5}{2}\right)}=\frac{2}{5}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(4,-11)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(-11)&=\frac{2}{5}(x-(4)), \\y&=\frac{2 x}{5} - \frac{63}{5}.
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=\frac{2}{5}x+\left(- \frac{63}{5}\right), \\x&=\frac{63}{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The intersection is $\left(\frac{63}{2},0\right)$.

Find where the normal line to the curve $y=-4\sqrt{x}-2x$ at the point with $x$-coordinate $1$ intersects the $y$-axis.

The intersection is $(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$. Give exact values.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First find the point on the curve.

$$
f(1)=-4\sqrt{(1)}-2(1)=-6.
$$

The normal passes through $(1,-6)$.

Rewrite the radical or reciprocal using powers, then differentiate.

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=- 4 x^{\frac{1}{2}} - 2 x, \\f'(x)&=-2 - \frac{2}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}}=-2 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{x}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(1)&=-2 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{(1)}}=-4, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{(-4)}=\frac{1}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(1,-6)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(-6)&=\frac{1}{4}(x-(1)), \\y&=\frac{x}{4} - \frac{25}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $y$-axis, $x=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=\frac{1}{4}\cdot 0+\left(- \frac{25}{4}\right), \\y&=- \frac{25}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The intersection is $\left(0,- \frac{25}{4}\right)$.
